# Test: wrap-aware enemy movement

Test-first verification slice for wrap-aware movement (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC3 + AC5). Pins per-edge wrapping for wrap-aware archetypes and the unchanged bounded behaviour of the classic exclusions.

## Goal

Specify, in tests, that wrap-aware motion which would carry an enemy off-screen wraps to the opposite edge while `march` and `centipede` keep their bounded, wall-respecting behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tests assert that crossing each of the four edges (left, right, top, bottom) relocates a wrap-aware enemy to the opposite edge, matching the player/asteroid four-edge wrap model (position only — velocity preserved).
- Tests cover the shared post-motion wrap helper in isolation (pure function, no Phaser) including the exact-boundary and multi-edge-overshoot cases.
- A test asserts `march` still reverses at the arena edge and drops vertically, and that `centipede` still weaves within bounds (`src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts` / centipede formation unchanged).
- A regression test asserts a non-aware archetype's position is never wrapped by the shared seam even when it leaves the arena bounds.
- At least one test covers each wrap-aware movement class (dive, chase, orbit, drift, roam, hold-and-move) at the seam.
- All tests pass deterministically.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
- `src/entities/Ghost.test.ts`
- `src/entities/Asteroid.test.ts`

## Acceptance Criteria

- The tests fail against the pre-change bounded/clamped motion and pass once the shared wrap lands.

## Problem statement

The PlayScene integration test `PlayScene — Robotron homing horde (AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6) > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`) failed once during the AI_Hell full suite (heavy machine load) and passed on a fresh full-suite re-run minutes later with identical code. It is a flaky test, not a gameplay regression, and it is the last remaining kill test in this file that has not been hardened against non-deterministic scene state.

## Users

- **AI agents and producers running the full suite** — a red full-suite gate blocks `dev` pushes and triggers `test-failure` triage items and retries.
- **Developers of the Robotron horde (and shared kill seam)** — they need the horde kill/accounting contract to stay proven while the test stays stable.

Example user stories:

- *As an agent whose `implement.py finish` gate runs the full suite, I want the Robotron horde kill test to pass deterministically so that an unrelated docs-only change is never blocked by it.*
- *As a maintainer, I want the wave-accounting contract (a horde kill counted exactly once) still asserted, so the fix does not hide a real regression.*

## Existing state (evidence)

Failure from the `implement.py finish` gate for AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H (docs-only change, cannot affect kill behaviour):

```
FAIL |integration| src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once
AssertionError: expected true to be false // Object.is equality
 ❯ src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6168:26
    6166|     scene.spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0);
    6167|     scene.tick(0.001);
    6168|     expect(victim.alive).toBe(false);
```

Same run also printed repeated `connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000` on stderr (unrelated noise; no test failed on it).

The current test body (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6174-6184`) is:

```ts
const victim = liveGrunts(scene)[0];
scene.spawnPlayerBullet(victim.x, victim.y, 0, 0);
scene.tick(0.001);
expect(victim.alive).toBe(false);
expect(wm.enemiesAlive).toBe(total - 1);
```

Two facts narrow the cause:

1. **The test is non-deterministic per run, independent of load.** `bootWithHordeWave()` never injects an RNG or run seed, so `PlayScene._initRunSeed()` draws a fresh `randomSeed()` (`Math.random()`, `src/core/rng.ts`) each run and the horde plan (`computeHordeSpawns`, `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts`) places the 16 grunts at RNG-jittered points along the four arena edges. The passing re-run therefore re-drew a different layout; "passed on re-run" is *not* evidence that load is the variable.
2. **The identical scenario has already been fixed one describe-block earlier.** `killing a pursuer advances wave accounting exactly once` (Pac-Man pursuer) had the same single-`tick(0.001)` shape and the same flake, and was fixed by wrapping the kill in the existing module-level `isolateEnemyForKill(scene, victim)` helper (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:397-410`, documented as AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK): it stubs `getEnemyEntities()` to the victim only and disables auto-fire for the duration, so "auto-fire or an overlapping pursuer cannot add a second kill and double-decrement the wave accounting". The Robotron horde kill test is the *unhardened sibling* of that test — it predates/omits the isolation.

The description's original hypothesis ("the physics/collision step for that tick may not process the new projectile before the assertion") is **not** supported: `scene.tick(dt)` is a synchronous call that runs the full player/auto-fire/bullet/collision/accounting pass in one go (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1265+`), so a longer tick cannot make a pass "complete"; what changes with a longer tick is *how much extra state* (auto-fire bullets, homing movement, wave timer) participates in that pass.

## Diagnosis to confirm during implementation

Confirm the exact mechanism before changing the assertion. Candidate mechanisms, in order of likelihood:

1. **Auto-fire / other-bullet interference** — the scene's auto-fire is live in this scenario, so a shot fired in the same tick can hit a grunt (or a different, overlapping grunt) and shift which entity the spawned bullet resolves against. The pursuer precedent (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) fixed exactly this with `isolateEnemyForKill`.
2. **Overlapping horde grunts** — grunts in one spawn group share an edge and can be placed close enough that a bullet placed on the victim is also within an earlier-iterated grunt's hit radius.
3. **Wave-phase/`paused` gating** — a wave-timeout transition switches `tick()` to the carried-survivor-only collision pass (`_handleCarriedSurvivorCollisions`), and a paused scene makes `tick()` a no-op; either would leave the victim alive. Check `scene.isTransitioning()` / `paused` under the failing seed.
4. **Wall-clock frames before the loop is stopped** — `bootScene()` resumes the live RAF loop, and `advanceGame()` stops it only after a microtask yield, so real frames with real deltas run before the deterministic stepping begins (load-dependent state drift). Relevant if the failure reproduces without seed isolation.

Reproduce deterministically (seed sweep): inject a fixed seed via `scene.setRng(createSeededRng(<seed>))` before `scene.restart()` and sweep seeds until the failure reproduces, then fix and verify that seed. Prefer the narrowest fix that removes the interference.

Steps to reproduce (seed sweep):

1. In `bootWithHordeWave()`, add `scene.setRng(createSeededRng(seed))` before `scene.scene.restart()` (import `createSeededRng` from `../core/rng`).
2. Loop seeds (e.g. `0..999`) in a temporary harness or repeated test-skill runs until `victim.alive` is `true` after the kill step; note the seed.
3. Record the seed and the observed mechanism on this work item, then apply the fix and re-verify that seed plus a broader sweep.

## Desired change

Make the horde kill test deterministic **without weakening what it proves**:

- Isolate the kill exactly as the pursuer test does — reuse `isolateEnemyForKill(scene, victim)` (`auto-fire` off, only the victim visible to the collision pass) — and/or pin the scene RNG to a fixed seed so the horde layout is reproducible.
- Keep the single-tick kill if it is deterministic after isolation; otherwise use a small bounded "tick until the victim dies" loop (guard counter, e.g. ≤ 20 frames of `0.016`) and assert the *outcome*.
- Still assert that the victim dies **and** that wave accounting drops by exactly one — and, to prove "exactly once", assert the accounting is unchanged after further ticks (no double decrement).

## Acceptance criteria

- The flaky failure is reproduced deterministically first (fixed seed and/or a temporary repeat-run harness), and the observed mechanism is recorded as a comment on this work item with the failing seed (or an explicit statement that no seed reproduces it, with the evidence gathered).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — Robotron homing horde > killing a grunt advances wave accounting exactly once` passes on repeated runs: at least 20 consecutive runs of `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` via the test skill, and at least one run with an additional concurrent load-generating job active, all green.
- The test still proves the contract: the victim grunt is dead after the kill step, and `wm.enemiesAlive` is exactly `total - 1` (and stays `total - 1` after further ticks — a kill is never counted twice). The "exactly once" proof is not weakened to "at most once".
- The fix is confined to test code (plus test comments); no gameplay behaviour, RNG semantics, or `isSpawning`/collision logic changes. If investigation shows a genuine gameplay defect is being masked, stop and record it as a new work item (`discovered-from:AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU`) rather than loosening the test.
- If the fix pattern is reusable (e.g. other horde/pursuer kill tests), note it in the test comment referencing AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU and AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK so the next reader sees why the isolation is required.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Test-execution policy:** every agent-initiated test run goes through the test skill (`/skill:test`, `run_tests.py`) — no ad-hoc `vitest`/`npm test`. Repeated-run verification is therefore a test-skill invocation with a narrow scope (changed-scope gate) plus the full-suite gate at push.
- **No assertion weakening:** a longer tick alone is acceptable only if it is deterministic after isolation; it must not become a "sleep until it works" loop with an unbounded guard.
- **No production-code behaviour change:** the horde kill path (`_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies`, `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`) is shared with every gym (`src/scenes/core/`), so a behavioural change would require gym-parity work — out of scope unless a real defect is found.
- Prefer reusing existing helpers (`isolateEnemyForKill`, `finishSpawnSequence`) over introducing a new pattern.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — horde kill test at ~6174; `bootWithHordeWave`/`releaseHorde` helpers at ~6089-6124; existing `isolateEnemyForKill` helper at ~397-410 to reuse.
- `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts` — RNG-driven spawn placement (`computeHordeSpawns`) explaining per-run layout variance.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `planHordeSpawns` / `_releaseDueHordeSpawns` (~2164-2245), `tick` collision/phase ordering (~1265-1390), `_initRunSeed` (~4849-4863).
- `src/core/rng.ts` — `randomSeed()` / `createSeededRng()` (`Math.random`-seeded runs by default).
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — `bootScene`/`advanceGame` deterministic harness (frame-loop stop/resume behaviour).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `_resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies` (~1189) and `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` (~384) — read-only context for the interference analysis.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** no gameplay defect is being masked. If the isolated test still fails for a fixed seed, the flake may reflect a real horde/accounting bug — escalate as a new (child) work item instead of widening the tick.
- **Risk:** adding `scene.setRng(...)` in this describe block changes the RNG stream for the other four horde tests in the same block; keep the seed pinned in a `beforeEach`-style helper or per-test so assertions like "spawns the configured horde" stay valid.
- **Risk:** a bounded tick loop can hide a regression that makes kills take longer; keep the bound small (≈ 0.32 s simulated) and assert exactly-once accounting afterwards.
- **Risk (scope creep):** other single-tick kill tests in the same file (asteroids, boss phases) use `tick(0.016)` and have not flaked; do not refactor them wholesale — record as separate work if desired.
- **Risk:** flake attribution — a green re-run under load is weak evidence; the fix must be justified by a *reproduced deterministic* failure, not by "it passed 20 times".
- **Risk:** `isolateEnemyForKill` stubs `getEnemyEntities` and `autoFireEnabled` on the instance and must be restored in a `finally` block (as the pursuer test does); a leaked stub would silently affect later tests in the same file.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK** (completed) — `[test-failure] PlayScene — flaky wave-accounting kill tests (Harvester + Pac-Man pursuer)`; introduced `isolateEnemyForKill` for exactly this interference class. Direct precedent.
- **AH-0MUNVVWWC0015JTM** (completed) — `Flaky tests: PlayScene and GymFormationScene fail intermittently under full-suite parallel load`; load-sensitivity remediation (deterministic boot/frames).
- **AH-0MV5JRAH90034PKR** (completed) — `Flaky Centipede chain bounds assertion under full-suite load`; fixed "advanced 20 s in one tick" by stepping in 0.05 s increments — precedent for tick-size fixes in this file.
- **AH-0MVFPMT4P005UHZL** — removed the last wall-clock waits from the suites (`advanceGame` / `stepGameUntil`); the deterministic harness this test relies on.
- **AH-0MV01EKTL001NRE6** — the Robotron homing horde feature these tests cover.
- **AH-0MVLJFCE6007T77H** (completed) — docs-only change whose gate surfaced this flake (`discovered-from`).
- `src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` — repo guard documenting the flake history and the supported deterministic replacements.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (agent consideration):** "Is the failure load-induced (wall-clock frame drift) or seed-induced (random horde layout)?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence, no producer input needed):** seed-induced is demonstrable from the code — `bootWithHordeWave` injects no RNG, so `_initRunSeed()` draws `randomSeed()` per run and `computeHordeSpawns` places grunts at RNG-jittered edge positions. The pass-on-re-run therefore used a different layout. Load may additionally drift scene state via live RAF frames before `advanceGame` stops the loop, but that is not required to explain the flake. Source: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4849-4863`, `src/core/rng.ts:49`, `src/waves/HordeSpawner.ts` (`computeHordeSpawns`).
- **Q (agent consideration):** "Does the description's proposed fix (`scene.tick(0.05)` / tick-until-dead) actually address the mechanism?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence):** only partially. `scene.tick(dt)` is synchronous, so "the collision step did not process the projectile" cannot happen; the pursuer precedent (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) shows the real interference was auto-fire / overlapping entities, fixed by `isolateEnemyForKill`. The brief therefore requires isolation (plus a fixed seed) as the primary fix, with a bounded tick loop only as a secondary robustness measure.
- **Q (agent consideration):** "Should the fix change gameplay code (e.g. horde collision ordering)?"
  - **Answer (resolved from repo constraints):** no. Any gameplay change is shared with every gym and would require gym-parity work; a genuine defect would be filed as a new work item instead. Assumption recorded in *Risks & assumptions*.
- **Producer input:** none required — the item's goal and acceptance criteria are unambiguous and the remaining decisions are resolved by repo evidence and precedent. Recorded here for auditability; no open questions.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUJRVYWG006NJUU** – Shared multi-hit kill finalisation (completed) — the shared kill seam this test's bullet path runs through.
- **AH-0MUIGTRFY002JDDS** – Shared mineral kill-drop helper + PlayScene/BaseEnemy refactor (completed) — touches the same enemy-kill finalisation path.

### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — gym↔game parity convention (§5.1), relevant to the "no behaviour change" constraint.
- `src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` — documents this flake family and the supported deterministic replacements.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — `isolateEnemyForKill` helper (AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK) reused by the fix.

---

## Plan (produced by /skill:plan on 2026-10-28)

Decomposition into 5 children in test-first dependency order (statuses shown at plan time; blocked children released for scheduling):

1. **Reproduce horde kill flake via seed sweep** (AH-0MVRLGUTZ007V3E5, task, high) — seed-injecting `bootWithHordeWave(seed?)` via `setRunSeed`, sweep seeds 0..999 until the un-hardened kill leaves the victim alive, record failing seed + mechanism comment; or record no-reproduction evidence. Satisfies AC1.
2. **Harden horde kill test with isolation** (AH-0MVRLGZPG0036ZTV, task, high) — `isolateEnemyForKill` with `finally` restore + fixed run seed; asserts victim dead, `enemiesAlive === total - 1` and stays so after further ticks (exactly once). Test comment references AH-0MVMEI9V1005H0LU + AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK. Satisfies AC3-AC5.
3. **Multi-seed horde kill regression guard** (AH-0MVRLH07H001KW8S, task, medium) — committed parametrised `it.each(≥50 seeds)` proving the exactly-once contract is layout-independent. Satisfies AC3 (durable).
4. **Document the horde kill isolation pattern** (AH-0MVRLH0P6004TNSZ, docs, medium) — test-file comment + flake-history docs (`src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts`, README/docs grep). Satisfies AC6.
5. **Verify hardened horde test under load** (AH-0MVRLH178001JITL, task, high) — ≥20 consecutive test-skill runs, one under concurrent load, failing-seed regression, full-suite green; evidence comment. Satisfies AC2, AC7.

Dependency edges: 2→1, 3→2, 4→2, 5→(3,4).

**Planning-time mechanism insight (candidate strongest):** `tick()` (src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1291-1341) switches to the carried-survivor-only collision pass when `transitionTimer > 0` (wave-timeout transition) — that pass never resolves a player bullet against horde grunts, leaving `victim.alive === true` and the accounting untouched for that tick. Whether the wave-timeout lands inside `releaseHorde`'s `tick(20)` vs the 0.001 s kill tick is seed-dependent because `HORDE_SPAWN_TIME_JITTER_SECONDS = 0.25` jitters spawn-group times. Confirmation/rejection is part of the reproduce step (checked via `scene.isTransitioning()` under the failing seed).

**Duplicate handling (plan session):** AH-0MVOKZ2WK006GLFF (open, idea stage, unassigned) described the same flake with ACs fully subsumed by this item's AC1-AC3 — closed as a duplicate during planning (comment + close recorded).

**Effort/risk:** parent estimate Small/Medium (effort_and_risk_skill, 2026-10-25) retained; per-child effort/risk set manually from it (S/Medium, S/Medium, S/Low, XS/Low, S/Medium) — re-running the skill per child was skipped to avoid duplicate report comments (idempotence).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers (plan session 2026-10-28)

- **Q (Map, planning):** "Which seed-injection seam should the reproduce harness use — `setRng(createSeededRng(seed))` (as the brief suggests) or `setRunSeed(seed)`?"
  - **Answer (Map, resolved from repo evidence):** `setRunSeed(seed)` is the canonical seam — `_initRunSeed` (src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:4903) reads the injected seed at the next `create()` and drives every gameplay draw, while `setRng` leaves the injected stream untouched and is documented for scripted-RNG tests. The plan therefore pins via `setRunSeed` before `scene.restart()`, with `setRng` as a fallback only if `setRunSeed` is shown not to drive the horde layout. (Child F1 AC1.)
- **Q (Map, planning):** "Is the wave-timeout transition branch a plausible mechanism for the flake, and should it be checked during reproduction?"
  - **Answer (Map, resolved from repo evidence):** yes — `tick()` gates the full collision pass behind `transitionTimer === 0`; a wave-timeout with grunts still alive switches to `_handleCarriedSurvivorCollisions`, which cannot kill a horde grunt. Spawn-time jitter makes the transition landing seed-dependent. Recorded as the planning-time mechanism insight above; F1 AC3 requires checking `scene.isTransitioning()`/`paused` under the failing seed.
- **Q (Map, planning):** "The idle open item AH-0MVOKZ2WK006GLFF covers the same flake — duplicate?"
  - **Answer (Map, resolved by AC comparison):** full duplicate — its ACs (rerun 5x, make assertion load-robust or document, declare verdict) are subsumed by this item's AC1-AC3; no work had started. Closed during planning. No producer input required (per intake Appendix).
- **OPEN QUESTION:** none — every remaining decision (isolation, seed pinning, bounded-loop guard, docs scope) is constrained by the parent ACs or resolved from repo evidence; the parent Appendix already records "no producer input required".

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-28 (Map, /skill:plan): claimed (already in_progress from intake); pre-check `plan-if-needed` → `plan`; approval gate → no approval pause (effort Small, risk Medium); created 5 children in test-first dependency order; wired dep edges; closed duplicate AH-0MVOKZ2WK006GLFF; ran the six automated review stages and the AC coverage review (coverage 100% → `proceed`); stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

# Shard Swarm — fire/impact VFX & SFX

**discovered-from:AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW** (5 net-new weapon types) — audit of the `shard_swarm` player weapon found it shipped with an in-flight bullet look only: no fire sound, no muzzle flash and no per-weapon impact feedback.

## Current state (audit evidence)

Present:
- In-flight identity: `bulletShape: 'shard'` + overrides (`bulletShapeLength: 1.6`, `bulletTrail: 1.2`, `bulletSize: 0.72`, lime `BULLET_COLORS.shard_swarm = 0xc0ff33`) in `src/utils/weapons.ts:1336`, rendered through the shared bullet-shape seam (`_shard` in `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts`).
- Code-drawn lime fan icon (`drawShardSwarmIcon`, `src/powerups/icons.ts:1121`).

Missing:
- **No fire SFX.** `playWeaponFireSound()` (`src/audio/effects.ts:628`) has no `shard_swarm` case, so it falls through to the `default:` no-op — the weapon fires silently in live play, in the hold-full metronome and in every gym.
- **No muzzle flash.** The definition declares no `muzzleFlash` metadata, and `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` (`src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts:896`) only spawns the launch cue `if (def.muzzleFlash)`.
- **No per-weapon impact feedback.** No `impactFx` spec, so `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx()` returns early: no baked hit cue (the impact is silent) and only the generic warm-white flash (`spawnBulletImpact`, `0xfff2a0`, r7, `CombatScene.ts:434`) rather than a lime shard-coloured one. The fan therefore reads as weak noise against the neon background at 0.72× bullet scale.

## Goal (user story)

As a player holding the Shard Swarm, I want an audible launch and hit so I can hear that the five-shard fan is firing and connecting, and I want the shards and their impacts to punch clearly against the neon field, so the weapon feels as distinctive in the hand as its silhouette suggests — without any change to its balance.

## Scope

`shard_swarm` only. Feel/visual/audio only — no behaviour or balance change: fire rate (750 ms, once per beat), the five offsets (±15°, ±7.5°, 0°), bullet lifetime (0.55 s → ~193 px reach), speed, size and colour stay exactly as they are.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Audible fire.** `playWeaponFireSound('shard_swarm')` routes to a new baked ToneForge fire cue (recipe `aihell-shard-swarm-fire`, rendered by `scripts/build-audio.sh`), so live fire, the hold-full metronome and gym fire all sound identical through the one shared path (`src/audio/effects.ts`, `PLAYER_WEAPON_IMPACT_CUES`-adjacent registry pattern).
- **Audible, visibly distinct impact.** `shard_swarm` declares an `impactFx` spec (`color` = lime-family, `radius`, `duration`, `cue`) resolved through `CombatScene.resolveWeaponImpactFx()`, producing a lime-tinted impact flash and a new baked hit cue (`aihell-shard-swarm-impact`) so the game and every gym connect identically. The generic white fallback flash no longer applies to this weapon.
- **Muzzle flash + more noticeable in-flight VFX.** The definition declares `muzzleFlash` metadata (lime, sized for a five-shard burst) spawned through the shared `CombatCoreScene._autoFire` → `spawnMuzzleFlash` path, and the shards are made more legible in flight (e.g. slightly stronger rim/spine contrast and/or a brighter trail) through the shared `bulletVisuals` seam — no per-scene copies, no new bespoke rendering path.
- **Gym↔game parity.** All changes land in the shared core/seams (`src/utils/weapons.ts`, `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts`, `src/vfx/`, `src/audio/`) and are consumed identically by `PlayScene`, `GymWeapons` and `GymWeaponLeveling`; `CombatScene.equivalence` and the gym-parity/documentation roster guards pass unchanged.
- **Docs + audio catalogue updated.** `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` records both new cues with their recipes and seeds, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` lists them, and the per-weapon visual roster guards (`src/utils/weaponVisualRoster.docs.test.ts`, `src/utils/bulletVisualRoster.test.ts`) plus README/GDD §4.4/§7.3 per-weapon notes include the Shard Swarm's fire and impact identity instead of listing it as visual-only.
- **No new legibility regressions.** The five-shard fan at full upgrade levels (extra projectiles, larger bullets) must not become a screen-filling blur: the impact/muzzle flashes are rate-limited by the natural 750 ms cadence and the effect sizes stay within the existing per-weapon effect budget.
- **Full test suite passes**, including new/updated tests for the fire cue dispatch, `impactFx` resolution, muzzle-flash spawn, and the audio cue contract test (`src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`).

## Key files

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `shard_swarm` `muzzleFlash` / `impactFx` metadata
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — ensure the new metadata survives level resolution
- `src/utils/bulletVisuals.ts` — in-flight `shard` legibility for the player weapon
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playWeaponFireSound` case + impact cue registry + `playShardSwarm*Sound` exports
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-shard-swarm-{fire,impact}.yaml`, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — shared spawn/impact seams (consume-only; no new hook needed if the metadata path suffices)
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, README, GDD §4.4 / §7.3

## Known sibling gap (not in this item's scope)

The same missing feel package (`muzzleFlash`, `impactFx`, fire cue) applies to the other four net-new unlock-pool weapons from AH-0MVCRC52P001YIPW: `rear_guard`, `broadside`, `railgun`, `heavy_slug`. Railgun SFX is already tracked by Railgun needs SFX (AH-0MVMIGVCE004VSNA); the remaining three have no item yet. The metadata/pipeline work here should be structured so those can reuse it unchanged.

## Risks / notes

- ToneForge assets are baked, not runtime-synthesised (`src/audio/thrusterShim.ts` is the sole runtime exception): new cues need recipe YAML + a `scripts/build-audio.sh` run, and the seeds must be recorded.
- Audio must remain a safe no-op in headless tests (no audio context).

# Make Phase Shift and wormhole-emergence effects unmistakable

## Problem statement

The improved Phase Shift / wormhole-emergence treatment shipped under
AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S (commits 4267a534, 4b407b66, eafc45b6, c84c1a99, 5b5877e4) is
technically complete and audited, but **the producer reports it is still not
noticeable enough — the effect must be unmistakable**. The intent of the original
epic ("instantly obvious that they are not in their usual state") is therefore not
yet satisfied in practice, even though every written acceptance criterion passed.

Producer feedback (2026-10-25, verbatim): *"These effects are not noticeable
enough, needs to be unmistakable."*

## Users

- **Player (primary):** "As a player, the instant my ship phases out — or enemies
  start materialising out of the wormhole — I want to *know* without looking for
  it. Not a tint I have to hunt for: an unmistakable event."
- **Player (defensive read):** "As a player relying on the automatic Phase Shift, I
  want the activation to read like a system event (a hit, a pulse, a distortion),
  not a subtle colour shift, so I can trust it and time my flying."
- **Developer / maintainer:** "As a developer, I want whatever stronger treatment we
  choose to live once in the shared VFX layer, stay toggleable per layer, and keep
  the gyms and the game pixel-identical."

## Current state (what shipped, and why it reads as subtle)

Screen-wide Phase Shift (`src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`):

| Layer | Current value |
|---|---|
| Dim overlay | dark blue 0x0a1a33, alpha 0.22 |
| Chromatic split | cyan 0x33ffee / red 0xff3355, **alpha 0.20**, base offset **6 px** (+/-1.5 px, 1.6 s) |
| Alpha flicker | 3 Hz, 25 % depth |
| Colour pulse | 0.75 -> 1.0 cross-fade |
| Activation burst | alpha 0.35 at +/-12 px, 200 ms fade |
| Camera shake | **deliberately none** (producer decision: it read like death juice) |

Per-enemy emergence (`src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` `updateEnemyShimmer`):
ripple burst +0.06 scale / +0.15 alpha over 200 ms, then alpha flicker 0.55-0.85 at
3 Hz, scale pulse 4 %, additive-bloom colour pulse (Phaser 4 `Container`/`Graphics`
have no Tint).

Wormhole ring (`attachWormholeRing`): 0xd9b3ff, r 52 px, 3 px stroke, alpha 0.45,
yoyo scale 0.9-1.15 every 900 ms.

Diagnosis of the shortfall (to be confirmed with the producer): every layer is a
**low-alpha translucent tint at screen-wide scale**, and translucency over a busy
bullet-hell background is perceptually weak. "Unmistakable" most likely needs
*high-contrast, structural* change — distortion, a hard flash, silhouettes, motion —
not just larger alpha values.

## Candidate approaches (producer to choose / amend)

**A — Bigger same-technique (lowest risk, no new rendering technique).**
Split alpha 0.20 -> ~0.45 and offset 6 -> ~14 px; burst alpha 0.35 -> ~0.70 at
+/-28 px over ~320 ms; add a short full-screen brightness flash on activation
(distinct palette from the death flash); add cyan edge/vignette bands during phase
(the defeat-screen vignette technique) so the *frame* changes, not just the objects;
per-enemy alpha flicker range widened (e.g. 0.25-1.0) plus a stroked silhouette
outline per emerging enemy; wormhole ring radius/alpha raised with an open shockwave.

**B — Real screen-space distortion via Phaser camera post-FX (highest impact).**
Use the engine's built-in post-FX pipelines on the main camera while phased: a
short displacement/pixelate wobble on the activation edge, then a sustained subtle
`Bloom`/`Glow` + gentle `Barrel`/`Displacement` wobble, all driven from the same
tunables. This is the genuine "glitch" read and is far more visible than alpha
tints. Caveats: the original epic explicitly scoped shader/render-to-texture work
out; needs a WebGL check + a headless-safe fallback, a measurable perf check, and a
canvas-renderer degradation path. Phaser post-FX state must also be torn down
exactly on the falling edge.

**C — Combination (recommended by the agent, producer decides).**
A for the player + wormhole (cheap, robust) **plus** B's activation-edge distortion
burst only (a ~150-250 ms pixelate/displacement hit), so the *event* is unmistakable
while the *sustained* state stays comfortable.

## Constraints

- **Gym<->game parity** (AGENTS.md): the behaviour lives once in `src/vfx/*` and the
  shared spawn path; `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and the combat gyms
  consume the same code. The duplicate-body guard and the gym-parity docs assertion
  must stay green.
- **No camera shake** unless the producer explicitly reverses that decision. (The
  regression test asserting "never shakes" currently encodes it.) If a shake-free
  "punch" is wanted, prefer camera **zoom** punch or post-FX over shake.
- **Seizure safety:** a genuinely unmistakable effect must still avoid rapid strobe.
  If flicker frequency rises, cap it (~<=3-4 Hz for sustained layers) and add an
  explicit accessibility toggle; a reduce-motion option remains a separate item.
- **Per-layer toggles and pure params model** are retained (`PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*`,
  `ENEMY_SHIMMER_ENABLE_*`, `WORMHOLE_RING_ENABLE`, pure `resolve*Params()`).
- **Headless-safe:** no-op without a Phaser render context; unit tests stay
  deterministic.
- **Performance-neutral to near-neutral:** no per-frame allocations; post-FX, if
  chosen, needs a measured cost check on the existing target hardware.
- **Visual distinctness from player-death juice** must be preserved and asserted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Player activation edge is an aggressive, structural glitch: a short camera-filter distortion burst plus a full-screen phase flash plus a wider chromatic surge.
- Player sustained state stays continuously obvious but soft: pulsing vivid split, cyan edge vignette bands, gentle sustained camera filter, no camera shake.
- Exact teardown: the falling edge removes every overlay, tween and camera filter, restoring the camera filter list with no residual state or duplicate layer.
- WebGL capability probe with graceful fallback: filter layers apply only when supported, otherwise degrading to overlay-only layers without throwing.
- Per-enemy emergence is unmistakable per entity: outline silhouette, stronger ripple burst, widened alpha flicker, fully restored when growth ends, no screen-wide overlay.
- Wormhole read: a brighter larger pulsing ring plus a one-shot open shockwave, tracked in wormholeEffects and fully cleared when the wormhole closes.
- Distinctness and parity preserved: visually distinct from player-death juice, never shakes the camera, gym-game parity guards green, headless no-op safe.
- Tests and docs: unit tests cover every new layer, teardown, fallback and the no-shake regression; GDD section 7.2 and code comments document all tunables; the full suite passes.

## Acceptance notes (detail per criterion)

1. **Activation edge (aggressive).** Rising edge fires, in the same frame: a ~150-250 ms camera-filter distortion burst (pixelate + barrel/displacement wobble), a full-screen flash in a phase-shift palette (never the player-death flash palette), and the widened/stronger chromatic-surge overlay pair. Every magnitude is an exported tunable; every layer has its own `PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*` toggle.
2. **Sustained state (soft).** Split alpha/offset raised and slowly oscillating, cyan edge/vignette band layer, gentle sustained filter layer; sustained flicker capped at <=3-4 Hz for seizure safety; no camera shake.
3. **Teardown detail.** A second expiry, a scene `SHUTDOWN` or a re-activation cycle leaves no residual tint, no leaked filter controller, no duplicated layer; pre-existing unrelated camera filters survive untouched.
4. **Fallback detail.** Renderer probe checks the WebGL renderer type and the camera filter list; unsupported renderers get the overlay-only layers with no error storm (headless/canvas tests exercise this path).
5. **Emergence detail.** Driven from the shared spawn path (`updateSpawnAnimation` -> `updateEnemyShimmer`) over the whole `ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION`; the entity's own alpha/scale/blend state is fully restored when growth ends.
6. **Wormhole detail.** One ring and one shockwave per wormhole; tweens stopped before destroy; registry cleared on close.
7. **Distinctness detail.** The no-shake regression test is retained; the duplicate-body guard (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity docs assertion stay green.
8. **Docs detail.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 7.2 plus JSDoc on every new exported constant and helper.

## Producer decisions (2026-10-25)## Producer decisions (2026-10-25)

- **Q1 = C** — combination: approach A (bigger same-technique + frame-level flash/vignette/silhouette) everywhere, **plus** approach B's screen-space distortion for the player path.
- **Q2 = iii** — aggressive on the activation edge, soft for the sustained state.
- **Q3 = no shake** — the no-camera-shake decision stands; the "punch" comes from post-FX/flash layers only. The existing regression test stays.
- **Q4 = ship and iterate** — the epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S is **not** held: no dependency edge from the epic to this item; it releases through the normal dev->main gate and this item improves the effect afterwards.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Which approach?** (A) bigger same-technique only; (B) real screen-space post-FX distortion for the player path; (C) combination.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **C**. Rationale: keep the robust overlay/vignette/silhouette work everywhere and add a genuine distortion read for the player's activation.
- **Q2 — How far may intensity go?** (i) comfortably strong; (ii) aggressive/startling; (iii) aggressive activation edge, soft sustained.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **iii**. Rationale: the *event* must be unmistakable; the *state* must stay comfortable for the whole phase duration.
- **Q3 — Revisit the no-shake rule?** (i) keep no-shake, use post-FX/flash instead; (ii) allow a short low-intensity shake on the activation edge only.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **no shake**. Rationale: preserves the established distinctness from player-death juice.
- **Q4 — Release hold for the epic AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S?** hold its release until this lands, or ship and iterate.
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-25): **ship and iterate**. No blocking edge is wired from the epic to this item.

## Technical feasibility note (verified before planning)

Phaser 4.2.1 exposes camera filters (`camera.filters.internal` / `.external`):
`addPixelate`, `addBarrel`, `addGlow`, `addVignette`, `addBlur`, `addParallelFilters`
(bloom), `addDisplacement`, `addColorMatrix`. They are **WebGL only**, so the driver
must probe `scene.game.renderer.type` / `camera.filters` and degrade to the
overlay-only layers otherwise. No post-FX is used anywhere in `src/` today, so this is
a new (but engine-supported) technique.

## Constraints

- **Gym<->game parity** (AGENTS.md): the behaviour lives once in `src/vfx/*` and the
  shared spawn path; `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and the combat gyms
  consume the same code. The duplicate-body guard and the gym-parity docs assertion
  must stay green.
- **No camera shake** unless the producer explicitly reverses that decision. (The
  regression test asserting "never shakes" currently encodes it.) If a shake-free
  "punch" is wanted, prefer camera **zoom** punch or post-FX over shake.
- **Seizure safety:** a genuinely unmistakable effect must still avoid rapid strobe.
  If flicker frequency rises, cap it (~<=3-4 Hz for sustained layers) and add an
  explicit accessibility toggle; a reduce-motion option remains a separate item.
- **Per-layer toggles and pure params model** are retained (`PHASE_SHIFT_ENABLE_*`,
  `ENEMY_SHIMMER_ENABLE_*`, `WORMHOLE_RING_ENABLE`, pure `resolve*Params()`).
- **Headless-safe:** no-op without a Phaser render context; unit tests stay
  deterministic.
- **Performance-neutral to near-neutral:** no per-frame allocations; post-FX, if
  chosen, needs a measured cost check on the existing target hardware.
- **Visual distinctness from player-death juice** must be preserved and asserted.

## Acceptance Criteria (draft — finalise after producer answers Q1-Q3)

- **Unmistakable activation read (player).** On the `isPhased` rising edge the
  treatment produces a structural, high-contrast change (not merely a tint): the
  chosen mechanism (A/B/C) fires within the same frame and is perceptible against a
  busy background in a manual play check; magnitudes exported as tunables with
  per-layer toggles.
- **Unmistakable sustained read (player).** While phased, the state remains
  continuously obvious for the whole duration (chosen sustained layer(s) from A
  and/or B), with the no-camera-shake guarantee intact and every layer torn down on
  the falling edge (no residual tint or residual post-FX state).
- **Unmistakable emergence read (enemies).** Each emerging enemy is individually
  obvious as "not solid yet" across its whole `ENEMY_GROWTH_DURATION` window, driven
  from the shared spawn path; the entity's own render state is fully restored when
  growth ends; no screen-wide overlay on the emergence path.
- **Wormhole read.** The open wormhole is clearly the source of the emergence (ring
  and/or column strengthened per the chosen approach), tracked in the existing
  `wormholeEffects` registry and fully cleared on close.
- **No regressions.** Death juice stays visually distinct; the no-shake regression
  holds (unless the producer reverses it, in which case it is updated deliberately);
  gym<->game parity guards pass; headless no-op tests pass.
- **Tests and docs.** Unit tests cover the new tunables/toggles, the new
  layers/mechanism creation + teardown (including post-FX teardown if chosen), and
  the no-shake and headless guarantees. `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 7.2
  and the code comments are updated with the final magnitudes. The full project test
  suite passes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — magnitudes, new layers, optional
  camera post-FX driver.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — per-enemy treatment, wormhole ring.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — shared driver (post-FX needs a camera).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` — consume the shared helpers only (no new behaviour).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` section 7.2 — final treatment + tunables.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S** (completed, audited, awaiting release) — the epic that
  delivered the current treatment. This item is `discovered-from:AH-0MV8BUKFK003Z23S`.
  The producer must decide whether the epic's release is held until this lands.
- AH-0MVD2MXAB004K0V4 — player phase-shift juice (vivid split + burst + shimmer).
- AH-0MVD2N333004VDA9 — per-enemy emergence shimmer.
- AH-0MVD2N6AW0073X5M — wormhole glow/pulse ring.
- AH-0MUJRGWGG0073JWS — original Phase Shift juice module (dim + split, no shake).
- AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB — end-of-run juice; the defeat glitch-flicker + vignette
  technique is the precedent for approach A's frame-level layers.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: seizure sensitivity / discomfort** — "unmistakable" pushes toward higher
  contrast and faster flicker. Mitigation: cap sustained flicker, keep the aggressive
  part on the short activation edge, keep per-layer toggles, and track a
  reduce-motion accessibility option separately.
- **Risk: post-FX complexity and platform variance** (approach B) — WebGL-only,
  needs canvas fallback, exact teardown, and a perf measurement. Mitigation: fall
  back to approach A layers when post-FX is unavailable.
- **Risk: parity drift** — mitigated by implementing once in the shared VFX layer;
  guards enforce it.
- **Assumption:** the producer's "unmistakable" means *perceptually unavoidable*,
  not necessarily *physically larger* — the chosen mechanism is a producer decision
  (Q1-Q3 above).

# Camera filter driver with WebGL capability probe

Shared infrastructure for approach C of AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU: Phaser 4 camera
filters are **WebGL only**, so every filter-based layer needs one guarded,
teardown-exact entry point.

## Goal

As a developer, I want a single shared module that can apply and clear the
Phase Shift camera-filter layers safely on any renderer, so the game and the
gyms never diverge and a headless/canvas build can never crash or leak.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Capability probe.** `supportsCameraFilters(scene)` returns true only when
  the renderer is WebGL *and* the camera exposes a usable filter list; it never
  throws for a stub, a missing camera, or a renderer without `type`.
- **Activation burst.** `applyPhaseDistortionBurst(...)` adds the pixelate +
  barrel/displacement wobble controllers for the documented duration, driven by
  the exported tunables (no hard-coded numbers).
- **Sustained layer.** `applyPhaseSustainedFilter(...)` adds the gentle
  sustained layer (low-strength glow/bloom or barrel) and returns handles for
  teardown.
- **Exact teardown.** `clearPhaseFilters(...)` removes and destroys only the
  controllers this module added, restoring the camera's pre-existing filter
  list unchanged (verified by a test that pre-adds an unrelated filter and
  asserts it survives).
- **Degradation.** When filters are unsupported every function is a documented
  no-op returning a falsy/"unsupported" result; nothing is allocated.
- **No per-frame allocation.** Steady-state updates mutate existing controller
  properties only.
- **Documented.** Module-level JSDoc explains WebGL-only behaviour, the fallback
  contract and every tunable.
- Player activation edge is an aggressive, structural glitch: a short camera-filter distortion burst plus a full-screen phase flash plus a wider chromatic surge. (enforced by the shared driver)
- WebGL capability probe with graceful fallback: filter layers apply only when supported, otherwise degrading to overlay-only layers without throwing. (enforced by the shared driver)

## Key Files

- `src/vfx/cameraFilters.ts` — new.
- `src/vfx/cameraFilters.test.ts` — new (see sibling test item).

# Intake Brief — Mini Boss explosions

**Work item:** AH-0MVOFGB6K003YD0Z (feature, high)
**Headline:** On mini-boss defeat, explode every remaining wave-gating enemy
(escorts plus the mini-boss's live minions) in a staggered sweep, add
`max(0, 30 − n)` extra explosions scattered at random across the scene plus 10
around the mini-boss's death point, and hold the mini-boss reward overlay until
every explosion animation has finished.

**Source request (verbatim):** "When the mini-boss it defeated all remaining
enemies should explode, add an additional 30 - # of enemies explosions
scattered randomly across the scene and 10 around the mini-boss. Do not show
the reward screen until all explosions have completed their animation."

## Problem statement

Defeating a mini-boss currently destroys only the mini-boss body (with its own
boss-scale explosion): surviving escorts and summoned minions stay on the field,
no celebration scatter fires, and the reward overlay opens on the same frame as
the kill — mid-explosion — so the defeat reads as abrupt rather than
celebratory. The operator wants a cascading explosion sweep on the defeat frame,
a short celebratory scatter, and the reward screen held back until the last
burst has finished animating.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, when I defeat the mini-boss I want every remaining
  enemy to blow up and an extra barrage of explosions across the screen, so the
  kill feels like a clear victory moment."
- **Player** — "As a player, I want the reward screen to appear only after the
  explosion display has finished, so I don't miss the celebration."
- **Developer/tester (gym)** — "As a tester I want the mini-boss gym's EXPLODE
  button to show the same sweep, so what I verify in the gym is what ships."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Remaining wave-gating enemies explode.** On the mini-boss's lethal
  hit, every live wave-gating enemy is destroyed in a staggered explosion sweep
  that begins on the defeat frame. Scope is **escort ships plus the mini-boss's
  live summoned minions**; non-blocking hazards (`asteroid`, `lane-traffic`, per
  `isNonBlockingHazard`) are **not** swept and remain on the field.
- **AC2 — Extra scattered explosions.** The sweep adds `max(0, 30 − n)` extra
  particle explosions, where `n` is the number of wave-gating enemies swept
  (escorts + minions), placed at positions sampled uniformly at random across
  the playfield, plus exactly **10** explosions clustered around the mini-boss's
  death position captured at destruction. Edge cases are explicit: `n = 0` → 30
  extras; `n = 30` → 0 extras; `n > 30` → 0 extras (never negative, never an
  exception). Total scattered bursts therefore never exceed 30.
- **AC3 — Reward screen waits for the explosions.** The mini-boss reward overlay
  (`MineralChoiceScene`, opened by `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward`) opens only
  after the last explosion burst in the sweep has completed its animation. The
  `miniBossRewardOpen` latch still opens exactly one overlay per defeat, and the
  demo auto-select contract (AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F) still applies after the delay
  (attract mode never stalls).
- **AC4 — Cosmetic-only destruction.** Swept enemies are removed from play but
  award **no score**, drop **no minerals / power-ups / Extra Life**, and emit
  **no kill telemetry**. Wave/level accounting still clears exactly once,
  **after** the sweep: the level advance never fires mid-display and never fires
  twice.
- **AC5 — Game↔gym parity.** `GymMiniBoss`'s EXPLODE path runs the **same**
  shared sweep helper as `PlayScene` (one implementation consumed by both); the
  repo duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the
  gym-parity docs assertion pass.
- **AC6 — Determinism and meaningful tests.** All random placement/jitter uses
  the run-seeded RNG (no `Math.random()` in the sweep), so a seed replays the
  same display; unit tests cover the count formula at the edges (`n = 0, 1, 29,
  30, 40`), the minion/hazard scope split, and the sweep-completion → overlay
  ordering (overlay does not open before the last burst finishes).
- **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries**
  (notably GDD §3.3/§4.4.4 and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`).
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Shared-code parity:** the sweep lives once in a new shared module under
  `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by `PlayScene` and `GymMiniBoss` — no
  divergent copy (AGENTS.md "Game Architecture Conventions").
- **Reuse the existing VFX:** explosions go through
  `spawnExplosionParticles` (`src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`) — same particle
  system, ~400 ms burst lifespan, shared per-kind VFX registry
  (`getExplosionVfxCounts`). No new particle system.
- **No reward of any kind** for swept kills (operator answer Q2 = B + C): this
  is celebration VFX only, so the mini-boss reward remains the single reward
  for the encounter.
- **Ordering:** the reward overlay's `setPaused(true)` would freeze the tween
  animations, so the sweep must be allowed to run and complete before the
  overlay pauses the scene.
- **Minion capture order:** mini-boss minions are owned by the `MiniBoss` entity
  and are currently torn down by `MiniBoss.destroy()` → `_clearMinions()`
  (plain `destroy(true)`, no explosion). The sweep must capture the live minions
  (e.g. `miniBoss.getMinions()`) **before** `miniBoss.destroy()`, otherwise they
  cannot be exploded or counted in `n`.
- **Demo mode** must remain non-blocking: the delayed overlay keeps the existing
  auto-select behaviour.
- **Determinism:** seeded RNG for placement/jitter, per the repo VFX contract.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene._damageMiniBoss` (~L2920): on the lethal hit captures a
  `MiniBossDefeatContext`, calls `miniBoss.destroy()` (which also clears
  minions), fires `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` (checkpoint + reward), then replays
  one destruction through the wave state machine with a stale-count
  reconciliation guard.
- `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` calls `openMiniBossReward` **synchronously** → the
  overlay launches and `setPaused(true)` runs on the defeat frame.
- Remaining escorts/survivors are not destroyed; minions are silently torn down
  with the boss body. Hazards (`isNonBlockingHazard`) are never wave-accounted.
- `MiniBoss extends Boss`; its own death already plays a boss-scale explosion.
  `BaseEnemy.destroySelf(scale?)` / `playExplosion(scale)` is the shared
  per-enemy explosion seam, and `destroySelf()` marks the entity dead without
  awarding anything — so a cosmetic sweep can reuse it directly.
- `GymMiniBoss` destroys via EXPLODE → `MiniBoss.takeDamage()` →
  `destroySelf()`; it has no reward overlay, so the gym shows the sweep only.
- Kill accounting lives in `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` (score → drops → wave
  advance); the sweep must **not** call that path (AC4).

## Desired change

Introduce a shared `miniBossDeathSweep` helper (pure planner + thin Phaser
executor) that:

1. collects the sweep targets — live wave-gating enemies (excluding
   `isNonBlockingHazard`) plus the mini-boss's live minions captured before the
   entity is destroyed;
2. staggers their `destroySelf()` explosions over a short window so the sweep
   reads as a cascade (a modest burst scale — enemy-scale, not boss-scale);
3. spawns the `max(0, 30 − n)` random scattered extras plus 10 bursts anchored
   at the mini-boss death position, all drawn through
   `spawnExplosionParticles` with the run-seeded RNG;
4. reports completion (last burst finished) so `PlayScene` then opens the
   mini-boss reward overlay; wave accounting advances once, after the sweep.

`GymMiniBoss`'s EXPLODE button calls the same helper (tests observe the burst
counts and completion).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/miniBossDeathSweep.ts` — **new** shared sweep planner
  (count/placement maths) + Phaser executor + completion callback, with tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_damageMiniBoss` (capture minions before
  `destroy()`), `_fireMiniBossDefeatHooks` / `openMiniBossReward` (defer the
  overlay until sweep completion), single deferred wave advance.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymMiniBoss.ts` — EXPLODE path consumes the shared sweep.
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` — reuse `spawnExplosionParticles` /
  `getExplosionVfxCounts`; add a completion-aware spawn option only if needed.
- `src/entities/MiniBoss.ts` — expose/retain live minions long enough for the
  sweep to explode them (e.g. a read-before-destroy accessor).
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — existing `destroySelf()` / `playExplosion(scale)`
  seams consumed by the sweep (no reward side effects).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — gym destroy seam used by the
  sweep in the gym.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§3.3, §4.4.4),
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — defeat-flow documentation.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` — parity guards that must keep passing.

## Related work

- AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z (completed) — mini-boss epic; this sweep refines its
  defeat behaviour.
- AH-0MVCRBISU006NUN5 (completed) — `PlayScene` mini-boss integration
  (`_damageMiniBoss` defeat path this change extends).
- AH-0MVCRAV3B0069AIJ (completed) — `WaveManager` per-level mini-boss gating
  (the wave-advance-once constraint).
- AH-0MVH85XXZ008INE2 (completed) — mini-boss left-behind graphics; precedent
  for tearing the encounter down cleanly on defeat.
- AH-0MVCRBNO6003E1CH (completed) — mini-boss reward overlay
  (`openMiniBossReward`, `miniBossRewardOpen`), the overlay this change delays.
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F (completed) — reward-overlay demo auto-select; must not
  stall behind the new delay.
- AH-0MVCB6LBE007I6R8 (open) — "Stop firing when boss is destroyed": related
  post-destruction cleanup pattern at the final boss; check for a shared
  "defeat moment" seam rather than duplicating gating logic.
- AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 / AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB (completed) — staggered
  multi-burst celebration scheduling (`spawnVictoryFireworks`) to mirror.
- AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY (open) — "Explosions sould be explosions": image-based
  explosion rendering; overlaps the VFX module but is orthogonal (visual
  quality vs defeat-sweep behaviour).
- AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V (completed) — the shared particle explosion module this
  change reuses.

Duplicate check: performed (keywords "explosions", "mini-boss", "reward
screen", "chain explosion") — **no overlapping completed item found**; the
nearest items (VFX quality AH-0MVJ8TB610098DSY, final-boss victory fireworks
AH-0MUWZ5HCV0034H44 / AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB) do not cover a mini-boss-defeat
explosion sweep.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** applies to the **mini-boss defeat only**. Extending the
  sweep to the final boss or ordinary wave clears is separate work (record as
  discovered work items, not scope).
- **Particle budget:** up to 40 bursts in a short window. Mitigation: extra and
  anchored bursts use a modest enemy-scale size/scale and a reduced particle
  count; the sweep is bounded by `max(0, 30 − n) + 10 + n ≤ 40` bursts.
- **Double-advance risk:** `_damageMiniBoss` already has a stale-count
  reconciliation that can replay `onEnemyDestroyed`; sweeping enemies changes
  the alive count, so tests must assert the level advance fires exactly once,
  after the sweep.
- **Minion teardown ordering** (see Constraints) — capture before destroy, or
  minions vanish without exploding and `n` is under-counted.
- **Pause ordering:** the overlay's pause freezes tweens; completion must be
  driven by real tween completion (or an explicit timer derived from burst
  lifespan + stagger), not by a frame count that could be frozen.
- **Assumption:** the 10 mini-boss bursts are anchored at the death position
  captured at destruction (same discipline as the victory fireworks anchor), not
  at the entity's (already destroyed) live coordinates.
- **Assumption:** "scattered randomly across the scene" means uniformly sampled
  within the playfield inset by the burst radius, so no explosion is clipped
  entirely off-screen. If the producer expects the full screen edge-to-edge,
  only the inset constant changes.
- **Assumption:** the sweep is a visual-only celebration; the mini-boss reward
  remains the only reward for the encounter (operator Q2 = B + C).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Per entry: question, answer, answering party, evidence.

- **Q1 (scope of "all remaining enemies")** — "Which live entities count as
  'all remaining enemies' and explode on the sweep: (a) everything alive on the
  field — escort ships, mini-boss-summoned minions, and hazards (asteroids, lane
  traffic); (b) wave-gating enemies only (escorts + minions, exclude hazards);
  or (c) escort ships only (exclude minions and hazards)?"
  — **Answer (operator): "1. B"** — wave-gating enemies only: escort ships plus
  the mini-boss's live minions; hazards (asteroids, lane traffic) are excluded
  and survive. Recommended option was (b); operator selected (b). Source:
  interactive reply. Research: `PlayScene.spawned` holds one entry per live
  entity including hazards; `isNonBlockingHazard`
  (`src/scenes/core/waveTimeout.ts`) is the shared hazard classifier, and
  `MiniBoss.getMinions()` exposes the entity-owned minions.
- **Q2 (kill semantics)** — "Should sweep-destroyed enemies be real kills — (a)
  full shared kill path (score, mineral/power-up/Extra-Life drops, telemetry)
  with wave-advance batched to sweep end; (b) cosmetic explosions only —
  enemies removed visually, no score/drops; or (c) destroyed without any reward
  or telemetry?"
  — **Answer (operator): "2. B + C"** — treat as (b) cosmetic explosions only
  **and** (c) no reward or telemetry: enemies are removed visually with their
  explosion VFX, and award no score, no mineral/power-up/Extra-Life drops and no
  kill telemetry (wave bookkeeping still updates so the level completes). Source:
  interactive reply. Recommended option was (a); operator overrode it with
  B + C. Research: `PlayScene._onEnemyKilled` is the reward-bearing path and
  must **not** be used by the sweep; `BaseEnemy.destroySelf()` marks the entity
  dead and plays its explosion only, so it is the correct seam.
- **Q3 (count formula edges)** — "With n remaining enemies, the spec says
  `30 − n` extra scattered explosions. When n ≥ 30 (or 0), what should happen:
  (a) clamp extra at 0 — total scattered bursts = `max(30, n)` from enemy bursts
  + extras, plus the fixed 10 at the mini-boss; (b) always fire at least 30
  scattered extras regardless of n; or (c) always fire exactly 30 scattered
  extras on top of the n enemy bursts (total `30 + n`)?"
  — **Answer (operator): "3. A"** — clamp the extra count at 0:
  `extras = max(0, 30 − n)`, so `n = 0` gives 30 extras and `n ≥ 30` gives none;
  the 10 mini-boss-anchored bursts are always additional. Source: interactive
  reply. Recommended option was (a); operator selected (a). Research: at a clean
  defeat `n` is usually small (escorts cleared first), but carry-over survivors
  and minions can push `n` higher, so the clamp keeps the display bounded
  (`total bursts ≤ n + max(0, 30 − n) + 10 ≤ 40`).

# Bot tuning scene is not using the same gameplay objects as the main game

## Problem statement

Gym scenes are the canonical parity reference for the shipped game, yet the
level-launch gym path (`GymLevel`, which `GymBotTuning` extends) carries its own
inline wave-spawn implementation that has drifted from `PlayScene`. A designer
tuning the bot therefore watches enemies that do **not** behave as they do in
play, which invalidates the tuning signal the gym exists to provide.

## Findings from repo investigation (intake, 2026-10-27)

The reported symptom is real and is one of several divergences in the same spawn
seam:

1. **Phasers spawn in a line then snap to their ring (reported bug).**
   `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1647`) and
   `GymFormationScene` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts:1755`) both
   resolve an orbital entity's wormhole-transit destination through the entity's
   live `formationSlot()` seam (AH-0MVEXVME1004SIIS). `GymLevel.spawnWave`
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts:299`) does not: its resolver returns the grid
   slot (`startX + driftX + col * spacingX`), so Phasers transit to a straight
   line and then snap onto the orbit when the spawn window ends. Because
   `GymBotTuning extends GymLevel` (`src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts:149`), the
   bot-tuning gym reproduces exactly the symptom the producer reported.
   Regression coverage exists for `PlayScene`
   (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6697`) and `GymFodderEnemies`
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts:396`) but **not** for
   `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning`.

2. **Launched-level enemies never fire.** `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` assigns
   `entity.shootEnabled = spawn.shootEnabled`; `GymLevel.spawnWave` never
   assigns it, and `BaseEnemy._shootEnabled` defaults to `false`
   (`src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts:97`), so every `tryFire*` method returns nothing.
   Campaign levels 4+ carry `shootEnabled: true`
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:157`), so a level launched from the curve editor or
   played in the bot-tuning gym is silently non-threatening. `GymLevel`'s own
   tests work around this by setting `victim.shootEnabled = true` by hand
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts:599`), which is itself evidence of the gap.

3. **March formations do not march.** `PlayScene` keeps a rigid `marchState`
   block and re-anchors march spawns (`_resetMarchFormation`,
   `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1737`); `GymLevel` has only horizontal `driftX`.
   Campaign levels 2–10 contain `march` groups
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:381-424`), so the launched block renders as a
   static line instead of the stepping/dropping block the game shows.

4. **The transit resolver is copied three times.** Each spawn site inlines the
   same non-trivial logic ("autonomous-mover exemption → orbital-slot branch →
   live slot / offset fallback"). The repo-wide duplicate-body guard
   (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`)
   does not cover this seam, which is why the third copy could drift unnoticed.
   `GymLevel` also keeps a legacy in-place spawn path used when no wormhole
   origin is supplied — dead for gameplay but still a second code path to keep
   honest.

5. **Divergences that must be preserved (already documented).** `GymPlayer`'s
   obstacle course, `GymWeapons`' AOE training targets, the flat supply cadence
   in `GymFormationScene`-derived gyms, gym-only HUD/tuning panels and the
   absence of run telemetry are intentional and recorded in
   `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 and `docs/BALANCING.md`. The
   fix must not "unify" these away.

## Users and example user stories

- **Bot-tuning designer (primary):** "As a designer tuning the bot in
  `GymBotTuning`, I want the enemies I watch to spawn, transit, march and fire
  exactly as they do in the shipped game, so the tuning I save transfers to the
  attract demo and recordings."
- **Gameplay developer:** "As a developer landing a spawn/formation fix in
  `PlayScene`, I want the gyms to consume the same seam, so I cannot leave a gym
  behind without the test suite failing."
- **Level/curve designer:** "As a designer launching a campaign level from the
  curve editor, I want the launched level to be a faithful preview of the
  shipped level."

## Existing state

- Three spawn implementations: `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (game),
  `GymFormationScene` (formation gyms), `GymLevel.spawnWave` (level/bot-tuning
  gyms). Only the first two honour the `formationSlot` seam.
- Spawn presentation (`startSpawnAnimation`, wormhole open/close, spawn
  protection) is already shared via `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`; what diverges is
  the **destination resolver**, the per-enemy `shootEnabled` hand-off and the
  march block.
- Gym↔game parity coverage is extensive for combat, drops, movement, boss
  motion and projectile lifecycle, but has no coverage for the start-of-wave
  spawn presentation on the level-launch path.
- The capture/scripted-scene seam (`src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts`) is already
  consumed by `GymFormationScene` and `GymLevel` only, and the scene registry
  (`scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`) already lists every `Gym<Name>` as capturable
  except the parameterised `GymFodderEnemies`/`GymLevel`.

## Desired change

1. Extract the wormhole-transit destination resolution into **one** shared
   helper under `src/scenes/core/` and make all four spawn sites
   (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss` minions) consume it,
   so the orbital-slot seam, the autonomous-mover exemption and the live-slot
   tracking can no longer drift.
2. Propagate the wave's per-enemy `shootEnabled` (and the formation RNG) through
   the `GymLevel` spawn path exactly as `PlayScene` does.
3. Bring the march block to the level-launch path (or consume the shared march
   state) so launched march waves step and drop as they do in the game.
4. Register the new seam in the duplicate-body guard and add cross-scene
   equivalence tests that boot `PlayScene` and `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning` with the
   same seeded orbital/march wave and assert identical spawn trajectories and
   identical fire cadence.
5. Sweep **every** gym scene (`src/scenes/gym/`, including the generic
   `GymFormationScene` and the level/bot-tuning path) against `PlayScene` for
   enabled-object parity and record the result in a single parity matrix. **Fix
   every real divergence found in this item** (each with a test), rather than
   deferring them; documented, intentional divergences stay, with their reason
   recorded in the matrix.
6. Adopt the scripted-scene `setup` seam in **every** gym in this item: each gym
   applies the shared `applySceneSetup` applier and exposes whatever
   scene-specific scenario parameters it needs (enemy roster, formation, level,
   toggles) through the capture scene config, so any gym can be driven from
   `examples/scenes.json` and recorded. Extend the config validation and the
   `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` / parameterised-scene contracts accordingly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Booting `PlayScene` and `GymLevel` (and therefore `GymBotTuning`)
      with the same seeded orbital wave produces the same per-frame transit
      target for every Phaser: each frame's destination equals the entity's live
      `formationSlot()`, and no enemy is ever placed on a straight line then
      snapped to the ring. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test that fails
      on the pre-change code (red-before / green-after).
- [ ] AC2 — A launched wave with `shootEnabled: true` fires in `GymLevel` /
      `GymBotTuning` at the same cadence and bullet speed as the same wave in
      `PlayScene` (shared dispatcher, real scene clock). Verified by a parity
      test, not a hand-set `shootEnabled` in the test.
- [ ] AC3 — A launched `march` wave steps/drops in the gym exactly as the game's
      block does for the same `dt` sequence. Verified by a parity test.
- [ ] AC4 — The spawn-transit destination logic is defined exactly **once**
      repo-wide, is registered in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`, and every spawn site
      (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss`) resolves to it;
      the duplicate-body guard fails if a copy is re-introduced.
- [ ] AC5 — A gym↔game parity matrix document records, for **every** gym scene
      under `src/scenes/gym/` (including the generic `GymFormationScene` and the
      level/bot-tuning path), which shipped gameplay objects it runs, whether it
      inherits the shipped start-of-wave/combat code, and — where it diverges —
      the reason. Every real divergence identified by the sweep is **fixed in
      this item** with a regression test; retained divergences are only those
      already documented as intentional and each is re-justified in the matrix.
- [ ] AC6 — Every gym applies the shared scripted-scene `setup` seam and exposes
      its scenario parameters through the capture scene config, so any gym can
      be launched and recorded from `examples/scenes.json`; the scene-config
      validator rejects unsupported/parameterised targets with a clear error, and
      the `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` registry contract and its pinning test are
      updated.
- [ ] AC7 — `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (and `AGENTS.md`
      § Game Architecture Conventions where the rule text changes) explain the
      shared spawn seam and point at the parity matrix; the docs guard test still
      passes.
- [ ] AC8 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
      including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site
      entries (including the scripted-scene/gym capture documentation).
- [ ] AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No balance changes. Behavioural differences introduced by this item must be a
  *fix toward* the game's behaviour, except where the producer explicitly asks
  for a new gym capability (scripted-scene setup, AC6).
- Must not "fix" documented intentional divergences (obstacle course, AOE
  practice targets, flat formation-gym supply cadence, gym HUD); each must keep
  its documented reason.
- Must not regress the automation that consumes the gyms: the capture CLI and
  `sceneSetup` appliers, Watch Demo / demo mode, the bot-tuning store, and the
  `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` registry contract.
- Scope is deliberately broad (producer direction: sweep and fix all in this
  item). If the sweep uncovers a divergence that cannot be fixed without a
  separate design decision, record it as a blocker with evidence on this item
  rather than silently expanding the design.
- The item is expected to be decomposed into child items at the plan stage
  (shared seam, spawn-parity fixes, gym sweep, scripted-scene adoption, docs);
  the ACs above are the whole-item contract.
- The reported symptom must be reproducible before the fix and demonstrably
  fixed after it (red-before / green-after per repo convention).
- Implementation runs in the item's own worktree per `AGENTS.md`.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` — **new** shared destination-resolver seam
  (orbital slot / offset fallback / autonomous exemption / live-slot tracking).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — consume the shared seam from `_spawnEnemy`;
  keep march state as the single source for block anchoring.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — replace its inline resolver.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` — consume the seam, propagate `shootEnabled` and
  the formation RNG, adopt the march block or document why not.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — inherits the fix; update its divergence
  note if the scenario description changes.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — minion spawn keeps the in-place (no-transit)
  behaviour through the same seam.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — register the new helper
  in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`; add cross-scene spawn equivalence coverage.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/levelParity.test.ts` — spawn/fire/march parity assertions.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§5.1) and a new gym parity matrix
  document (e.g. `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`) listing every gym scene, the shipped
  objects it runs and its divergences.
- `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` — docs guard update if the rule text
  changes.
- `src/scenes/core/sceneSetup.ts` — extend the applier so every gym can take a
  setup; `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` and its tests — extend the config schema,
  parameterised-target handling and `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS` contract.
- `src/scenes/gym/*.ts` (all 14 gym scenes, including `GymCurveSequencer`,
  `GymPlayer`, `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUps*`, `GymWeaponLeveling`,
  `GymPowerUpLeveling`, `GymMinerals`, `GymCentipede`, `GymMiniBoss`) — apply the
  setup seam and fix any divergence the sweep finds.
- `examples/scenes.json` and `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — demonstrate a
  scripted scene for each gym family.

## Related work

- Wormhole/transit/formation-slot lineage: AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW (enemies emerge
  from the wormhole), AH-0MVDW3T9R0054HG6 (transit movement, parity, docs),
  AH-0MVDW3R7300979DC (scene-level transit tests), AH-0MVEXVME1004SIIS (Phasers
  spawn in a line then snap), AH-0MVF4P31M0033RAC (shared orbital geometry and
  orbital transit destination), AH-0MVF4OVY6000DZE8 (orbital geometry tests),
  AH-0MV8BR9Y70079TKC (wormhole placement), AH-0MV9KHLV8006GMX6 (wormhole
  lifecycle).

# Test: cross-scene spawn/fire/march parity for the level-launch path (red-before)

Parent: AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV (AC1, AC2, AC3). **Test-first item — create and land the failing tests before any production change.**

## Goal / user story

As a gameplay developer, I want a cross-scene equivalence test that boots `PlayScene` and the
level-launch gym (`GymLevel`, and `GymBotTuning` through inheritance) with the *same* seeded wave
and asserts identical spawn transit, identical fire cadence and identical march motion, so a
future divergence in the spawn seam cannot land without the suite failing.

## Problem

Parity coverage today exists for `PlayScene` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts:6697`) and
`GymFodderEnemies` (`src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts:396`) but **not** for the
level-launch path. `GymLevel.test.ts` even works around the missing `shootEnabled` hand-off by
setting `victim.shootEnabled = true` by hand, which is itself part of the defect.

## Required behaviour (the assertions that must exist)

1. **Orbital transit destination (AC1).** For an orbital wave (the Phaser), every frame of the
   wormhole spawn window in `GymLevel` must resolve a destination equal to the entity's live
   `formationSlot()` — asserted frame by frame against the same wave driven through `PlayScene`.
   No frame may place the Phaser on the straight grid line `startX + driftX + col*spacingX`, and
   the landing position at the end of the window must equal the orbital slot (no snap).
2. **Fire cadence (AC2).** A launched wave with `shootEnabled: true` must produce the same number
   of bullets, at the same `scene.time.now` ticks, with the same bullet speed, in `GymLevel` /
   `GymBotTuning` as in `PlayScene`. The test must **not** set `shootEnabled` by hand — it must
   flow from the wave definition (`src/waves/Formations.ts`, campaign levels 4+).
3. **March block (AC3).** For a `march` wave, stepping through an identical `dt` sequence must
   produce the same base position (x, y, direction) and the same per-member offsets in `GymLevel`
   as `PlayScene`'s `marchState` block, including at least one edge reversal and one drop.

- Put the new coverage in `src/scenes/gym/levelParity.test.ts` (already the level-gym parity home,
  AH-0MVLJF6ZD00164MG) unless the file becomes unwieldy, in which case add

  equivalence patterns in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and
  `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` — do not invent a second harness.
- Express the wave with a fixed seed so both scenes see identical content (the `sceneSetup` seed
  seam, `resolveSetupSeed`). No `Math.random`.
- Mark the new assertions with Vitest `it.fails(...)` (the repo's red-before/green-after
  convention, cf. `levelParity.test.ts` header) **or** `it(...)` with an explicit
  `// red-before: fails until AH-<child-of-this-item> lands` note, and flip them to `it` in the
  fix item. Whichever convention the surrounding file already uses must be followed.
- The flip-to-green work belongs to the implementation children (shared seam
  AH-0MVRMHQC9003VDNN, then the `GymLevel` parity fix AH-0MVRMHSKH0066J9B). This item is complete
  as soon as the tests exist and demonstrably fail on the pre-fix HEAD; the red-before markers are
  flipped by AH-0MVRMHSKH0066J9B.

## Red-before evidence

Record in a comment: the exact failing assertion output on pre-fix HEAD (all three assertions),
plus the commit hash of the test-only commit. This is the reproducibility proof the parent ACs
require.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A cross-scene test asserts, frame by frame, that `GymLevel`'s orbital spawn
  destination equals the live `formationSlot()` for every frame of the spawn window, and that the
  end-of-window position equals the orbital slot; it fails on pre-fix HEAD and the failure output

Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test that fails on the pre-change code (red-before / green-after). — **contribution:** this item delivers the red-before cross-scene test half (see Parent AC coverage below).
