# Shared wormhole-transit destination seam, consumed by all four spawn sites

Parent: AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV (AC4, and prerequisite for AC1). **Pure refactor: behaviour must not
change in any scene.**

## Goal / user story

As a gameplay developer, I want the wormhole-transit destination resolution defined exactly once,
so that the game and every gym consume the same "autonomous-mover exemption → orbital live slot →
grid-slot/offset fallback" rule, and a re-introduced copy fails the suite.

## Problem

The resolver is currently inlined three times:

- `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1647`) — the reference behaviour
  (`formationSlot` seam + `marchState` base + `driftX`).
- `GymFormationScene._spawnFormation` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts:1755`) — same
  rule, portal-based base, no march.
- `GymLevel.spawnWave` (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts:299`) — a **divergent** copy that returns the
  grid slot and therefore reproduces the reported "Phaser spawns in a line then snaps" symptom.
- `GymBoss` minion spawn (`src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts:274`) — no resolver at all (in-place).

The repo-wide duplicate-body guard (`EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` in
`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) does not cover this seam, which is why the third
copy could drift unnoticed.

## Desired change

1. New module `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` exporting **one** resolver, e.g.
   `resolveSpawnTransitTarget(...)`, which takes the narrow structural inputs it needs and returns
   `{ x, y }` or `undefined` (meaning "no transit — spawn in place"):
   - the entity (read structurally for `autonomousPositioning` and optional `formationSlot`);
   - the base position for this frame (march base when the wave is a march block, else
     `startX + driftX`, `startY`);
   - the formation `offset` and the group `spacingX` / `spacingY`.
   The resolver owns the rule only — it must not import Phaser, must not read scene fields, and must
   not mutate the entity.
2. Consume it at **all four** spawn sites. Each site keeps its own *base* computation (the game's
   `marchState`, the formation gym's portal, the level gym's launched drift, the boss's in-place
   exemption) — that is scene structure, not the rule.
3. `GymLevel` consumes the seam with **unchanged** behaviour in this item (it will still pass its
   grid-slot base, because it has no march/formation-slot wiring yet); the behaviour fix lands in
   the follow-up `GymLevel` parity item. This keeps this item a verifiable no-op refactor.
4. Register the resolver in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` in
   `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` with the canonical definer path, and extend the
   guard fixture so a re-introduced copy is proven to fail (the guard already has a
   "detects a re-introduced duplicate" describe block to extend).

## Implementation guidance

- Keep the ordering of the existing rule exactly: **autonomous → orbital live slot → grid offset**.
  The orbital branch must call `formationSlot.call(entity, baseX, baseY)` so the entity's own
  geometry stays authoritative (AH-0MVF4P31M0033RAC, AH-0MVEXVME1004SIIS).
- Preserve every existing comment's intent by moving the rationale into the new module's header
  (the "never appear in a line then snap onto the ring" reason) and leaving short pointers at the
  four call sites.
- Prefer a structural input type over importing entity classes, so the module stays pure and the
  gyms can pass their own shapes.
- Do not "fix" the `GymLevel` behaviour here; the red-before tests from the parity-test item must
  still fail after this item lands.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` exists, is Phaser-free (importable in a node-only
  unit test), and defines the transit destination rule exactly once.
- [ ] AC2 — `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel` and `GymBoss` all resolve their transit
  destination through that single helper; no site re-implements the orbital/autonomous/offset
  branch chain.
- [ ] AC3 — The helper is registered in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` in
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, the single-definer guard passes, and the
  guard's duplicate-detection fixture covers the new helper.
- [ ] AC4 — Unit tests for the new helper cover: autonomous mover → `undefined`; orbital entity →
  live `formationSlot` result (including a slot that differs from the grid slot); non-orbital
  entity → grid slot from base + offset × spacing; march base vs drift base input handling.
- [ ] AC5 — Every pre-existing test passes unchanged (no behaviour change): scene behaviour is
  identical before and after the refactor, verified by the existing PlayScene, GymFormationScene,
  GymBoss and GymLevel suites plus the equivalence suite.
- [ ] AC6 — The red-before parity tests added by AH-0MVRMHJZS001Z6CX still fail after this item
  (proving the refactor alone does not "fix" the bug).

- AC4 — The spawn-transit destination logic is defined exactly **once** repo-wide, is registered in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS`, and every spawn site (`PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymLevel`, `GymBoss`) resolves to it; the duplicate-body guard fails if a copy is re-introduced. — **contribution:** this item delivers it in full (see Parent AC coverage below).

## Key files

- `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts` (new) and `src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`_spawnEnemy`)
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (`_spawnFormation`)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` (`spawnWave`)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` (minion spawn)
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (`EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` + guard fixture)

## Constraints

- No behaviour change in any scene; this item is reviewed as a refactor.
- No balance change.
- Must not touch the documented intentional divergences (obstacle course, AOE targets, flat
  formation-gym supply cadence, gym HUD, no telemetry).

# GymLevel / GymBotTuning spawn parity: orbital transit, shootEnabled, march

Parent: AH-0MVP5IGX5005XTVV (AC1, AC2, AC3). This is the **behaviour fix** that turns the
red-before parity tests green.

## Goal / user story

As a designer tuning the bot in `GymBotTuning`, I want the enemies I watch to spawn, transit, march
and fire exactly as they do in the shipped game, so the tuning I save transfers to the attract demo
and to recordings.

## Problem (three divergences in one seam)

1. **Phasers spawn in a line then snap to their ring.** `GymLevel.spawnWave` (`src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts:299`)
   resolves the transit destination as the grid slot (`startX + driftX + col*spacingX`), while
   `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` and `GymFormationScene` resolve it through the entity's live
   `formationSlot()`. Because `GymBotTuning extends GymLevel`
   (`src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts:149`), the reported symptom reproduces there.
2. **Launched-level enemies never fire.** `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` assigns
   `entity.shootEnabled = spawn.shootEnabled`; `GymLevel.spawnWave` never assigns it, and
   `BaseEnemy._shootEnabled` defaults to `false` (`src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts:97`), so every
   `tryFire*` returns nothing. Campaign levels 4+ carry `shootEnabled: true`
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:157`), so a launched level or bot-tuning run is silently
   non-threatening. `GymLevel.test.ts:~599` works around this by setting `shootEnabled` by hand.
3. **March formations do not march.** `PlayScene` keeps a rigid `marchState` block and re-anchors
   march spawns (`_resetMarchFormation`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1737`); `GymLevel` has only
   horizontal `driftX`. Campaign levels 2–10 contain `march` groups
   (`src/waves/Formations.ts:381-424`), so a launched block renders as a static line.

## Desired change

1. **Orbital destination.** Feed the shared `resolveSpawnTransitTarget` seam
   (`src/scenes/core/spawnTransit.ts`, from AH-0MVRMHQC9003VDNN) the correct per-frame base so
   an orbital entity's transit target is its live formation slot, not the grid line. Do **not**
   keep a second branch in `GymLevel`.
2. **shootEnabled + formation RNG.** Propagate `group.shootEnabled` onto each spawned entity exactly
   as `PlayScene` does, and thread the formation RNG (`createEnemyFromConfig`'s rng argument) the
   same way the game does, so per-enemy randomness in the gym is the game's randomness. Remove
   reliance on hand-set `shootEnabled` in `GymLevel.test.ts` and assert the hand-off instead.
3. **March block.** Adopt the shared march module (`src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts` —
   `createMarchState`, `computeMarchBounds`, `advanceMarch`, `marchSpeedMultiplier`, already
   consumed by `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene`) on the level-launch path so a launched march
   wave steps, reverses and drops as the game's block does, and march spawns re-anchor to the block
   base during transit. Do not copy `PlayScene`'s block-mutation code — if `PlayScene`'s march
   bookkeeping is itself scene-specific, extract only what is genuinely shared and document the
   remainder; a second march implementation is not acceptable.
4. Keep the launched-level preview honest: the gym must not regress its existing level scaling /
   supply-cadence parity (AH-0MVLJF6ZD00164MG) or the force-field resolution at the launched level
   (AH-0MVM8GXEF009883O).

## Implementation guidance

- Prefer a small `GymLevel`-local march holder that owns `MarchState` + `MarchOptions` for the
  active wave, mirroring `PlayScene._resetMarchFormation` / its per-tick advance, but call the
  shared pure `advanceMarch` — the policy stays shared, only the holder differs. If the holder
  logic is identical to `PlayScene`'s, extract that holder (a class or factory) into
  `src/scenes/core/` and register it in `EPIC_SHARED_HELPERS` rather than duplicating it.
- `GymLevel` spawns a whole `WaveDefinition` per launch and re-spawns on level launch; reset the
  march state exactly where `PlayScene` resets it (per wave), not per enemy.
- `GymBotTuning` inherits the fix; only its divergence note (if it describes the scenario) needs
  updating.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Booting `PlayScene` and `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning` with the same seeded orbital wave
  produces the same per-frame transit target for every Phaser: each frame's destination equals the
  entity's live `formationSlot()`, and no enemy is placed on a straight line then snapped to the
  ring. The red-before test from AH-0MVRMHJZS001Z6CX is flipped to green by this item.
- [ ] AC2 — A launched wave with `shootEnabled: true` fires in `GymLevel`/`GymBotTuning` at the same
  cadence and bullet speed as in `PlayScene` through the shared dispatcher (`fireForEnemy`), with
  the flag flowing from the wave definition — the hand-set `shootEnabled` in `GymLevel.test.ts` is
  deleted and a test asserts the hand-off from the wave/spawn descriptor.
- [ ] AC3 — A launched `march` wave steps, reverses and drops identically to the game's block for
  the same `dt` sequence (parity test green).
- [ ] AC4 — `GymLevel`'s transit destination contains no orbital/autonomous branch of its own — it
  resolves through the shared seam (statically asserted by the duplicate-body guard).
- [ ] AC5 — Existing level-gym parity is preserved: `levelParity.test.ts` (scaled counts, supply
  cadence) and the force-field tests still pass, and a manual/scripted check of a launched
  campaign level shows firing and marching enemies.
- [ ] AC6 — No balance change: the fix makes gym behaviour match the game, and the game's behaviour
  is unchanged (verified by the untouched `PlayScene` suite).

- AC1 — Booting `PlayScene` and `GymLevel` (and therefore `GymBotTuning`) with the same seeded orbital wave produces the same per-frame transit target for every Phaser: each frame's destination equals the entity's live `formationSlot()`, and no enemy is ever placed on a straight line then snapped to the ring. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test that fails on the pre-change code (red-before / green-after). — **contribution:** this item delivers the behaviour-fix half that makes the test green (see Parent AC coverage below).

- AC2 — A launched wave with `shootEnabled: true` fires in `GymLevel` / `GymBotTuning` at the same cadence and bullet speed as the same wave in `PlayScene` (shared dispatcher, real scene clock). Verified by a parity test, not a hand-set `shootEnabled` in the test. — **contribution:** this item delivers the shootEnabled hand-off that makes the test green (see Parent AC coverage below).

- AC3 — A launched `march` wave steps/drops in the gym exactly as the game's block does for the same `dt` sequence. Verified by a parity test. — **contribution:** this item delivers the march adoption that makes the test green (see Parent AC coverage below).

## Key files

- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` (`spawnWave`, march holder, per-tick update)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` (divergence note only)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.test.ts` (remove the hand-set `shootEnabled` workaround)
- `src/scenes/gym/levelParity.test.ts` / new `spawnParity.test.ts` (flip red→green)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (reference behaviour only — must not change)
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` (`shootEnabled`, `march` groups)

## Constraints

- Behaviour changes must be *toward* the game; never change `PlayScene` to match the gym.
- Do not regress the capture CLI, Watch Demo / demo mode, the bot-tuning store, or the

question: May we add a new baked SFX cue, or must we reuse an existing one?

Options:
- (a) **New dedicated recipe** (`aihell-orbital-strike`) + baked WAV built via `scripts/build-audio.sh`.
- (b) **Reuse an existing electric recipe** (e.g. `aihell-arc-fire`) — no new asset.
- (c) No new audio; make the visual carry the identity.

**Recommended:** (a) — an orbital strike is a signature event and should not share a cue with the arc weapon.

Constraint either way: `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`, `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` and the audio contract tests (`src/audio/effects.contract.test.ts`, `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`) must be updated in the same change.
